source: codebook_v4 + сравнение модели с эталоном 24.09.2026: разведены цена и монетизация, сеттинг и тема в атмосфере, кража контента в поведении компании. Заморожен: дальнейшие правки только по отложенной выборке других жанров

categories.name: Overall
categories.definition: General evaluations of the game that do not single out a specific dimension of quality.

subaspects.name: Overall impression
subaspects.definition: A holistic judgment of the game, including nostalgia and comparisons with other games. Use only when the review gives no specific reasons.

categories.name: Monetization and value
categories.definition: Judgments about the financial relationship between the player and the game, including pricing, purchases, and business ethics.

subaspects.name: Pricing fairness
subaspects.definition: Judgment of a specific price: the game or a paid add-on is too expensive, fairly priced, or worth it on sale.

subaspects.name: Monetization practices
subaspects.definition: How the company extracts money from players: microtransactions, battle passes, splitting the game into paid add-ons, pressure to keep paying.

subaspects.name: Content access model
subaspects.definition: Whether content is unfairly locked behind payment, removed, vaulted, or rotated away from players who previously had access.

subaspects.name: Business conduct
subaspects.definition: Company decisions and attitude toward players and the game: priorities, ethics, treatment of fans, plagiarism or stolen content, regional restrictions, bans, corporate strategy.

categories.name: Technical performance
categories.definition: Judgments about how well the software runs.

subaspects.name: Frame performance
subaspects.definition: Frame rate, loading times, hardware demands, and optimization.

subaspects.name: Stability
subaspects.definition: Bugs, crashes, glitches, save corruption, and other technical errors during play.

subaspects.name: Connectivity
subaspects.definition: Network connection quality, server availability, login reliability, and offline functionality.

categories.name: Challenge and difficulty
categories.definition: Judgments about how the game calibrates challenge, handles failure, and introduces complexity.

subaspects.name: Enemy and boss difficulty
subaspects.definition: How hard the game is against the player: enemy and boss health, damage, challenge level, too hard or too easy.

subaspects.name: Punishment design
subaspects.definition: How the game penalizes failure (death penalty, item loss, lost progress) and whether it feels fair.

subaspects.name: Learning curve
subaspects.definition: How well the game explains its systems, guides new players, and ramps up complexity.

categories.name: Progression and engagement
categories.definition: Judgments about the sense of advancement and whether the game respects the player's time.

subaspects.name: Progression pacing
subaspects.definition: The rate and satisfaction of character, account, or skill advancement.

subaspects.name: Grind and repetition
subaspects.definition: Whether required activities are tediously repetitive, padded, or demand excessive time investment.

subaspects.name: Reward satisfaction
subaspects.definition: The quality, excitement, and fairness of loot, drops, and earned rewards.

categories.name: Presentation
categories.definition: Judgments about the audiovisual and atmospheric qualities of the game.

subaspects.name: Visual quality
subaspects.definition: Graphics, art direction, animations, and overall visual appeal.

subaspects.name: Audio quality
subaspects.definition: Music, sound effects, sound design, and voice acting.

subaspects.name: Atmosphere, setting and theme
subaspects.definition: Mood, sense of place and immersion, including the game's setting and theme (mythology, era, genre fantasy).

categories.name: Narrative and world
categories.definition: Judgments about storytelling, world construction, and structured content like quests.

subaspects.name: Narrative quality
subaspects.definition: Story, writing, lore, and characters.

subaspects.name: World design
subaspects.definition: The physical game world only: map layout, environments, and exploration. Not the amount of content and not access to areas.

subaspects.name: Quest design
subaspects.definition: The quality and variety of missions, objectives, and structured activities.

categories.name: Core systems
categories.definition: Judgments about the feel and balance of the game's main interactive systems.

subaspects.name: Combat feel
subaspects.definition: Responsiveness, satisfaction, and physicality of combat and action controls.

subaspects.name: Class and weapon balance
subaspects.definition: Balance between player options: classes, weapons, builds, strategies, or PvP sides. Not the player versus enemies.

subaspects.name: Build depth
subaspects.definition: Variety and meaningfulness of character customization, skill choices, and strategic options.

subaspects.name: Non-combat systems
subaspects.definition: Building, crafting, farming, fishing, taming, trading, and other non-combat activities.

categories.name: Play modes and social
categories.definition: Judgments about playing alone or with others and about the online social environment.

subaspects.name: Solo experience
subaspects.definition: How enjoyable and viable the game is when played alone.

subaspects.name: Multiplayer experience
subaspects.definition: The quality of playing cooperatively or competitively with other people.

subaspects.name: Community quality
subaspects.definition: Behavior, toxicity, and overall health of the player community.

subaspects.name: Matchmaking quality
subaspects.definition: How well players are paired by skill, interest, or connection quality.

subaspects.name: Anti-cheat
subaspects.definition: How well the game detects, prevents, and handles cheating and exploitation.

categories.name: Development and support
categories.definition: Judgments about the ongoing stewardship of the game by its creators.

subaspects.name: Update quality
subaspects.definition: The polish and effect of patches and changes, including updates that break or worsen the game.

subaspects.name: Development pace
subaspects.definition: Speed and direction of ongoing development, including prolonged early access.

subaspects.name: Developer communication
subaspects.definition: Public statements, announcements, roadmaps: transparency and honesty of what the developers say.

subaspects.name: Customer support
subaspects.definition: Help with a specific account, purchase, or technical problem through support channels. Not the general attitude of the company.

subaspects.name: Mod support
subaspects.definition: Whether the game supports player-made modifications and how the developers treat modding.

subaspects.name: Game lifecycle
subaspects.definition: End of service, server shutdown, sunset of live content, or announced end of development.

categories.name: Usability
categories.definition: Judgments about how easy and comfortable the game is to interact with.

subaspects.name: Interface design
subaspects.definition: Menus, HUD, inventory management, and convenience features that reduce friction in everyday play.

subaspects.name: Control scheme
subaspects.definition: Comfort, intuitiveness, and responsiveness of input and keybindings.

subaspects.name: Accessibility
subaspects.definition: Settings and options for players with different physical needs: subtitles, colorblind modes, remapping, and similar.

subaspects.name: Localization
subaspects.definition: Quality and availability of translation, subtitles, and voice-over in the player's language.

categories.name: Content design
categories.definition: Judgments about the amount, freshness, and replayability of what the game offers.

subaspects.name: Content volume
subaspects.definition: The amount of content relative to price or expectations.

subaspects.name: Content variety
subaspects.definition: Diversity of activities, environments, and experiences.

subaspects.name: Endgame depth
subaspects.definition: Availability and quality of meaningful activities after the main content is complete.

subaspects.name: Replayability
subaspects.definition: Incentive and enjoyment of replaying content or starting new playthroughs.

subaspects.name: Originality
subaspects.definition: How fresh and innovative the game feels compared to alternatives in its genre.
